cards.front: Recall a key point about Hobbies and Interests
cards.back: This topic covers key vocabulary and structures for hobbies and interests. You need to know the topic vocabulary, be able to use it in all four skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), and express opinions with reasons.

cards.front: What should you know about french exam tips — hobbies and interests?
cards.back: 1. For Hobbies and Interests, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Hobbies and Interests, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
reading (e.g. J'adore la lecture — I love reading)

cards.front: What does la bande dessinée (la BD) mean?
cards.back: comic book (e.g. Les BD sont très populaires en France — Comics are very popular in France)

cards.front: What does jouer du piano mean?
cards.back: to play the piano (e.g. Je joue du piano depuis trois ans — I've been playing piano for three years)

cards.front: What does le pass Culture mean?
cards.back: cultural pass (€300 for 18yr olds) (e.g. J'ai utilisé mon pass Culture pour des concerts — I used my pass Culture for concerts)
club/society (e.g. Je fais partie d'une association — I'm part of a club)
photography (e.g. Je fais de la photographie — I do photography)

cards.front: What does le Festival d'Angoulême mean?
cards.back: Angoulême comic festival (e.g. Le Festival d'Angoulême est le plus grand festival de BD — The Angoulême Festival is the biggest comic festival)

cards.front: What does le rap français mean?
cards.back: French rap (e.g. Le rap français est très populaire — French rap is very popular)
traditional drumming (Sénégal) (e.g. Le sabar est une tradition sénégalaise — The sabar is a Senegalese tradition)

cards.front: What does les jeux vidéo mean?
cards.back: video games (e.g. Je joue aux jeux vidéo le week-end — I play video games at the weekend)
choir (e.g. Je chante dans la chorale — I sing in the choir)
to relax (e.g. La musique me détend — Music relaxes me)

Students often forget to use the perfect tense for completed past activities. Wrong: Hier, je joue au foot. Correct: Hier, j'ai joué au foot (perfect tense for completed past actions). Students also mix up à and en with countries. Wrong: Je vais à France. Correct: Je vais en France (en with feminine countries starting with consonant).
